title: Incremental checkpointed schema and tool-call replay acceptance
creator: Asha Gupta
description: Context: Customers are adopting streaming structured responses with mid-stream tool invocations for multi-step workflows. We need deterministic behavior when partial JSON frames are emitted, schema fields evolve across model versions, and downstream services or the gateway retry tool-calls. This ticket scopes acceptance criteria for a compact incremental checkpoint protocol appended to streamed frames, compatibility rules for schema evolution, and deterministic tool-call replay semantics (idempotency and unique-call affinity) during retries and partial replays. Objectives: unambiguous developer guarantees for runtime, gateway, SDKs; QA validation across hosted and Dedicated deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint metadata: Every streamed structured frame MUST be optionally accompanied by a single-line checkpoint envelope when enabled. Envelope keys: checkpoint_id (uuid v4), seq (monotonic integer per response), stable_prefix_hash (hex), final: true|false. Checkpoint envelope MUST be parseable without buffering the full stream.

Resume API: SDKs expose resume(checkpoint_id, seq) to request frames from seq+1. The server MUST be able to return the minimal delta frames required to deterministically reconstruct the final object given checkpoint_id and starting seq.

Schema evolution rules: Field additions are allowed as optional. Field removals require a deprecation transition: removed fields map to explicit null-with-deprecation-code in emitted streams for at least one major runtime release. Type changes (number<->string) require a nullable wrapper step before hard-change. Compatibility rules must be published in Console model catalog.

Tool-call idempotency: Tool invocations emitted during a stream MUST include tool_call_id (uuid v4) and idempotency_hint (sha256 of normalized args). On retry, runtime must guarantee at-most-once execution for tool_call_id if the tool reported completion acknowledgement. If a previous execution completed but response was lost, runtime MUST return the original tool response for the same tool_call_id for up to 24 hours or 10000 seq units.

Deterministic replay: When a client requests replay from checkpoint N, tool calls with seq <= N MUST NOT be re-executed. Tool calls with seq > N MUST be re-emitted in identical order and with identical idempotency_hint. Non-idempotent side effects must be flagged; SDK resume() must require explicit opt-in to re-execute non-replayable actions.

Partial-error frames and backpressure: If runtime detects sustained queue growth beyond SLO thresholds, it MUST emit a structured partial-error frame with error_type, retry_after_seconds (optional), and checkpoint_id pointing to last stable seq. SDKs must present this as a resumable error with wait or replay-from-checkpoint options.

Observability: Every checkpoint envelope and tool_call event MUST include trace_id and span_id compatible with OpenTelemetry. Console must reconstruct full request timelines via checkpoint_id and tool_call_id for debugging and replay analysis.

QA test harness: Integration tests must demonstrate (a) successful resume from mid-stream of a 12-frame streamed object, (b) schema removal via deprecation path preserving deterministic merge, and (c) deterministic tool-call replay with a mock idempotent external tool. Tests must run against hosted and a Dedicated replica with identical vectors.

SDK and docs: Acceptance requires SDK additions resume(checkpoint_id), onPartialFrame(callback), toolCallAck(tool_call_id) and Console doc page describing checkpoint semantics, schema evolution rules, and recommended tool integration patterns.

Metrics and dashboards: Add metrics stream.resume.success_rate and toolcall.duplicate_rate. Acceptance requires baseline collection in staging and Console dashboard panels for one week prior to GA signoff.
notes: Decision: Adopt a minimal line-oriented checkpoint envelope (plain UTF-8 line) instead of a binary header to reduce parsing complexity on small clients.
Trade-off: Storing deterministic tool outcomes increases persistence cost. Chosen heuristic: retain outcomes for 24 hours or 10000 seq units to bound cost while covering typical retry windows.
Follow-up: Explore cross-region checkpoint lookup for multi-region Dedicated customers in a future iteration.

Edge case: For tool-calls with non-deterministic side effects (e.g., third-party charge), SDK must surface a 'non_replayable' flag and include telemetry. Product to decide default behavior for non-replayable actions (block resume by default or require explicit override).
